candidate: NEXT_PROMPT.md (2026-08-23 planning pass) Candidate 1: the CEX/DEX funding spread, Hyperliquid vs Binance
hypothesis: A funding-rate spread between an on-chain perp venue (Hyperliquid) and a large CEX (Binance) is a structurally different, more one-signed return driver than a funding LEVEL (018) or a CEX-vs-CEX funding SPREAD (020's Binance/Bybit, which found none worth having). The mechanism offered is structural, not a data artefact: an on-chain venue's flow skews retail/directional, a large CEX's is institutional/two-sided, and institutions find a DEX hard to onboard to, so the gap should not be competed away the way 020's CEX-vs-CEX spread was. This notebook tests that against real Hyperliquid data for the first time in this repo.

hyperliquid_new.round_turn_derivation: 2 * ((PERP_TAKER_BP+SLIPPAGE_BP) + (HL_TAKER_BP+SLIPPAGE_BP)) = 2*((5.0+1.0)+(4.5+1.0)) = 23.0 -- same fully-costed convention as bl20.ROUND_TURN_BP_XV (25.0bp for Binance/Bybit), so the two are directly comparable. The 19bp bare-fee figure from the planning survey is NOT used as a book's cost -- it excludes slippage and would be inconsistent with every other book in the repo.
hyperliquid_new.dev_start_derivation: matches Probe P1/P2's own window exactly (Hyperliquid's BTC history begins mid-2023, well after 018/020's 2021-07-01 start) -- so pre-registered gates are computed on the identical dev window the planning-time probe numbers came from, not a superset that would silently re-run the probe under new conditions.

configurations.HL_ALWAYSON: timed=False: every liquid symbol held every bar, direction=sign(carry), no floor, no position cap. The pre-registered HEADLINE -- NEXT_PROMPT.md's design implication that always-on is a live candidate for the first time in this programme, because the spread is 72% one-signed with a structural story, unlike every previous always-on variant (A_alwayson -0.415, cross-venue always-on -1.869).
configurations.HL_TIMED_FAST: timed=True, bl20's own THETA_IN_XV/THETA_OUT_XV (45-period/~15-day target hold), N_MIN_HL floor, MAX_POSITIONS_HL cap. Falsification comparator: if this is needed to clear HD-2 while HL_ALWAYSON does not, that is evidence against the structural story and is reported as such regardless of which way HD-2 goes.
configurations.HL_TIMED_SLOW: timed=True, THETA_IN_HL_SLOW/THETA_OUT_HL_SLOW (90-period/~30-day target hold), same floor/cap. A middle ground between the two, at the programme's own already-adopted 'slow carry' cadence (020's TARGET_HOLD_SLOW).

HD-1.fires_iff: pooled mean gross hlvenue_paired_log_return (fixed w=+1 direction: short HL/long Binance) across all liquid symbol-bars > 0 with Newey-West |t| > 3, lag=CARRY_EWMA_HALF_LIFE

HD-2.claim: the headline book (HL_ALWAYSON) is tradeable -- restates FA-2's three legs verbatim, as RC-2/XD-2 did in 020
HD-2.fires_iff: net Sharpe > 0.5 at every origin offset in [0,1,2,3] AND the 95% block-bootstrap CI on mean net per-bar return excludes zero AND deflated_sharpe_prob(...) > 0.95 at n_trials=12 (see n_trials_itemisation)

HD-3.claim: the dev window is adequately powered to detect an effect of the size the planning probe suggested -- written before Phase 4 runs, per 021's lesson that the power calculation goes first, not last
HD-3.fires_iff: the pooled gross spread series' own annualized Sharpe exceeds the closed-form MDE at 80% power / 5% two-sided, computed via power_lib21.bootstrap_se_from_ci + power_lib21.mde from that series' own 95% block-bootstrap CI. Planning-time estimate: MDE (annualized Sharpe) approx 1.98 over 2,190 8h bars / 2.0 years -- this notebook recomputes it from its own data rather than reusing the estimate.

HD-4.claim: genuinely neutral, not a disguised directional bet -- restates RC-4/XD-4
HD-4.fires_iff: |beta| to the equal-weight crypto basket and to BTC both < 0.10, at every origin offset, for HL_ALWAYSON

HD-5.claim: the result is not solely episodic / carried by one or two symbols -- mandatory per NEXT_PROMPT.md's 'the mean exceeds the median' flag, mirroring 020's own drop-top-2 fragility finding
HD-5.fires_iff: after dropping the 2 symbols with the largest total net PnL contribution to HL_ALWAYSON over the dev window, net Sharpe remains > 0 AND the 95% block-bootstrap CI on mean net per-bar return still excludes zero

HD-6.claim: fast timing is not required to make the numbers work (falsification check on the structural story) -- DESCRIPTIVE, no pass/fail bar

HD-7.claim: the result survives a long-tail slippage stress, not just the flat 23bp cost -- a proxy for the un-modelled per-symbol slippage NEXT_PROMPT.md flags as the highest-risk piece of engineering here
HD-7.fires_iff: net Sharpe of HL_ALWAYSON remains > 0 at a stress round-turn cost of 40bp (roughly 1.7x the pre-registered 23bp), applied flat across all symbols -- explicitly disclosed as a stress-cost proxy, not a modelled slippage curve calibrated to each symbol's own book depth

JELLY.claim: descriptive only, NOT a pass/fail gate -- what did HL_ALWAYSON's realized net return do through the 2025-03-26 Hyperliquid JELLY force-settlement event (validator-voted administrative settlement of a perpetual to protect the platform's own vault; vault TVL fell ~$540M to ~$150M). JELLY itself is not in this notebook's universe (not Binance-listed), so this reports the BOOK's realized return in the surrounding window as a platform-risk characterisation, not a JELLY-specific trade outcome.

implementation_notes.sign_convention: A=Hyperliquid, B=Binance throughout (basis_lib22.py module docstring). carry = EWMA(hl_funding_rate - binance_funding_rate); carry>0 means Hyperliquid funding is the more expensive side (the structural prior), and w=+1 is short Hyperliquid perp / long Binance perp.
implementation_notes.dsr_call_shape: identical to 020's own (basis_lib18.book_metrics -> research._series_metrics -> per-period, non-annualized Sharpe; skew=scipy.stats.skew(returns, nan_policy='omit'); kurtosis=scipy.stats.kurtosis(returns, fisher=False, nan_policy='omit')). fisher=False, non-excess kurtosis -- the single easiest way to produce a plausible-looking wrong number, per 020's own note, repeated here verbatim because the risk is identical.
implementation_notes.top2_symbol_selection: ranked by each symbol's own summed net_log_return contribution (weight * fwd_hlvenue_paired_return_1, net of that symbol's own share of turnover cost) over the full dev window on HL_ALWAYSON, computed once before HD-5 is scored, not re-tuned to find the worst pair.
implementation_notes.gate_json: every gate verdict is written to JSON as a boolean per leg, not just the conjunction.

n_trials_itemisation.convention: as in 020/021, n_trials for deflated_sharpe_prob counts BOOK/BACKTEST CONFIGURATIONS scored, not every descriptive statistic computed along the way. The pre-registration-preceding probes (below) are disclosed separately because NEXT_PROMPT.md's own planning pass explicitly charges them to whichever notebook picks up Candidate 1, but they are not Sharpe draws over comparable book configurations and are not folded into this number -- exactly 021's own treatment of its non-Sharpe trials ('no DSR consumer').

holdout_policy.1: the Hyperliquid dev-window holdout (2025-07-01+) is NOT pre-fetched anywhere in this repo, unlike basis18/holdout and bybit20/holdout -- it is freely fetchable from the same public, unauthenticated endpoint Phase 1b already used. The fence here is a matter of discipline, not of what is on disk (NEXT_PROMPT.md's own warning, taken literally): no script in this notebook other than a dedicated, not-yet-written run_phase_6_22_holdout.py may ever pass an end date past research.HOLDOUT_START to any Hyperliquid fetch function, and run_phase_1b_22_fetch_hyperliquid.py's own _assert_within_dev_window has no override parameter at all -- it refuses unconditionally.
holdout_policy.2: HL_ALWAYSON unlocks holdout access iff HD-2 AND HD-4 AND HD-5 all fire. No partial credit.
holdout_policy.3: at most one holdout pass, ever, running HL_ALWAYSON only (the headline; HL_TIMED_FAST/SLOW do not get holdout access even if HD-6's comparison is favourable to them, since they were never gated on their own terms).
holdout_policy.4: if built, run_phase_6_22_holdout.py must itself fetch the 2025-07-01+ Hyperliquid data it needs (nothing is cached) -- and is the only file in this notebook permitted to do so.
holdout_policy.5: after a holdout run, the notebook closes. No dev-side re-runs, no parameter changes, no one more variant.
holdout_policy.6: if no gate fires, run_phase_6_22_holdout.py is not built at all this round -- unlike 020 (which had pre-cached holdout data to prove refusal against), there is nothing to refuse against here, so a placebo refusal run is not applicable.

fallback_policy.hl_api_unreachable: retry with the existing 3x exponential backoff (5s/10s/15s); if still unreachable after that, the symbol/window is recorded as a fetch error in the Phase 1b manifest, not silently skipped.
fallback_policy.thin_universe: if fewer than 20 symbols have >=1 year of usable, liquid, jointly-available Binance+Hyperliquid dev-window overlap, the notebook is recorded as 'not runnable at pre-registered scope -- data blocker' (009's idiom) and ships with whatever descriptive Phase 2/3 work (HD-1, HD-3) completed.
fallback_policy.no_substitution: a thin universe or missing symbol is a clean, reportable outcome. An improvised replacement (different venue, different fee assumption, different window) is an unregistered trial.
